reviewed logic; raised scoping question and suggestions

claims.text: Alters -acceptnonstdtxn beyond expected behavior originated in Knots where upgradable opcodes are not enabled
claims.quote: Seems like this goes beyond the expected behaviour. Maybe make it =2 at least?
claims.status_note: luke-jr pushed back in c:2155749633 arguing that Knots behavior is the correct thing to follow
claims.status_by_quote: Whether you are required to or not, it is the correct thing to do. This option originated in Knots where it has always been available on mainnet, and expected to not enable upgradable opcodes/etc.

claims.text: Make CheckInputScripts generic and return validation state/ScriptError to callers rather than passing caller context
claims.quote: I think the second commit adds some brittleness to the CheckInputScripts function; it now needs to know whether we are in block validation or individual transaction validation.
claims.status_note: ismaelsadeeq clarified they were not rigid and deferred to consensus
claims.status_by_quote: I’m curious to hear other reviewers' thoughts, though, not rigid on this at all. Just bringing up ideas here.

claims.text: Return TX_CONSENSUS rather than TX_NOT_STANDARD on non-block input script consensus failure
claims.quote: I think after this PR, in non-block input script validation path, the result enum after a consensus input script failure is TX_NOT_STANDARD, which is incorrect; it should be TX_CONSENSUS.
claims.status_note: author explained current policy-first design and ismaelsadeeq agreed it made sense
claims.status_by_quote: Yeah, fair point, but worth noting that in that case, it makes sense we hit the policy first

claims.text: Limit scope by not modifying CheckInputScripts arguments and letting failures report as block errors when acceptnonstdtxn is off
claims.quote: One suggestion that limits the scope a bit: just don't change the CheckInputScripts args, so the report per-tx message turns into "block-*" if it's a block validation related script failure when standardness knob is off?
claims.status_note: instagibbs accepted author's rationale regarding chaintip differences
claims.status_by_quote: Ok this difference vs actual chaintip is persuasive against my idea

claims.text: Update the log message in ConsensusScriptChecks on failure
claims.quote: The log message in ConsensusScriptChecks on failure is a little off after this patch.

claims.text: Assert the property later in the function instead of just having a comment
claims.quote: can we assert this property later in the function instead of just a comment?
claims.status_note: author implemented compile-time and runtime checks in update c:5044185650
claims.status_by_quote: Compile-time check to ensure that `STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS` covers everything that `GetBlockScriptFlags` might return

claims.text: Use an enum instead of a boolean for CheckType to distinguish block and mempool checks
claims.quote: I have a slight preference for making this an enum, which seems more in line with communicating whether it is either block or mempool, like you state in the commit title.
claims.status_note: author introduced an enum in push noted in rc:3629106380
claims.status_by_quote: Made it an enum, but chose a slightly different name for it.

claims.text: Check that GetBlockScriptFlags returns a subset of STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS in a unit test rather than introducing a type change
claims.quote: It still seems confusing to me to introduce this type change here in a function that has nothing to do with standardness. Is this check really required in the first place? Maybe the invariant "GetBlockScriptFlags returns a subset of STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS" can just be checked in a unit test instead?
claims.status_note: sedited accepted the change and suggested resolving
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks, feel free to resolve this.

claims.text: Use a unit test instead of a compile-time check in GetBlockScriptFlags
claims.quote: I am not sure we need this compile-time check and I think I would prefer a unit test as it seems easier to understand and maintain.
claims.status_note: fjahr came around to compile-time check after trying alternatives
claims.status_by_quote: I've come around to the current approach of the compile time check but only after trying other approaches myself.

claims.text: Remove unused constants right away instead of leaving them for a follow-up, or add a comment
claims.quote: I would slightly prefer that we clean this up already and remove the unused constants right away instead of leaving them for a follow-up.
claims.status_note: author noted merge conflict risk and reviewer agreed follow-up is fine
claims.status_by_quote: that one is fine for me to keep for a follow-up.

claims.text: Move the Assume into GetBlockScriptFlags at the end where the comment is added
claims.quote: I think it would be better to move this `Assume` into `GetBlockScriptFlags` at the end where you are adding the comment.

claims.text: Add a release note for the change
claims.quote: Oh, and this should probably get a release note.

claims.text: Assert that std_reject is not None in p2p_invalid_tx test template
claims.quote:
std_reject = template.std_reject_reason or template.reject_reason
            assert std_reject is not None
claims.status_note: author explained the test exercises an orphan accepted when relayed but rejected in block
claims.status_by_quote: This change wouldn't be correct -- `BadInputOutpointIndex` tests something that's accepted as an orphan when relayed, but rejected when included in a block.

claims.text: Whether the risk on testnet is qualitatively different from existing standardness checks failing
claims.quote: To check: Risk seems similar to what already can happen on testnet if any of the other standardness checks fail? Just now with script interpreter things?
claims.status_note: author detailed the difference in behavior when soft-fork activation occurs
